content.theory:
HTML stands for **HyperText Markup Language**. It is not a programming language — it's a *markup* language. You label pieces of content (headings, paragraphs, links, images) so the browser knows how to display them. A page is built from **elements**, each written as a **tag**: ```html

Hello, world!

``` - `

` is the **opening tag** - `Hello, world!` is the **content** - `

` is the **closing tag** (note the slash) Most elements have an opening and a closing tag. A full HTML page wraps everything in a few structural tags: ```html My Page

Welcome

``` - `` tells the browser this is HTML5 - `` holds meta info like the `` (shown in the browser tab) - `<body>` holds everything visible on the page **Attributes** add extra info to a tag. They live inside the opening tag: ```html <a href="https://example.com">Visit</a> ``` Here `href` is an attribute with the value `https://example.com`.
